stage: HISTORIE (engine stage 6) - fractal axis + competing frames - cache
disputedNote: Even where this story begins is disputed - picking a start date is itself a position. Frames change emphasis and annotation, never the record.

frames.label: Oct 2023
frames.note: Story opens with the Oct 7 Hamas attack and Hezbollah's cross-border barrages a day later. Under this frame, today's US strikes on Iran and Israeli operations in south Lebanon read as the spreading edge of a single war that began in late 2023. This is the frame US and Israeli officials and most Western broadcasters open with.

frames.label: 2006 Lebanon war
frames.note: Story opens with the 2006 Israel-Hezbollah war and the blockade and reconstruction years that followed. Under this frame, current Israeli strikes on Tyre, Sidon and south Lebanon read as the resumption of an unfinished Lebanon conflict, not a Gaza spillover. This is the frame Lebanese papers, Al Jazeera and Arab regional outlets open with.

frames.label: 1979 revolution
frames.note: Story opens with the 1979 Iranian revolution, the US embassy crisis and the rupture of US-Iran relations. Under this frame, the current US strikes and Iranian retaliation read as the latest chapter of a 47-year US-Iran confrontation that has run through Lebanon, Iraq and the Gulf. This is the frame Tehran, TASS and many non-aligned analysts open with.

bands.label: Open US-Iran exchange
bands.summary: US launches strikes on Iran, an American Apache helicopter is downed near Hormuz, Iran vows it will not hesitate to defend itself and Israeli strikes kill dozens in south Lebanon as Trump threatens further attacks.

nodes.title: US Apache helicopter goes down near Strait of Hormuz
nodes.what: A US Army Apache helicopter was downed near the Strait of Hormuz on June 10, with American forces moving to recover the crew. Trump said Iran had admitted involvement in the attack and cited it as justification for escalating US action.
nodes.disputed: Trump describes Tehran as admitting to the strike on the Apache; Iranian statements frame the wider clash as US aggression and do not echo a confession.

nodes.title: Trump says US will hit Iran 'hard' as peace talks stall
nodes.what: Trump announced on June 10 that the US would launch fresh harsh strikes on Iran in the coming hours, accusing Tehran of 'playing us for suckers' after negotiations stalled. The New York Times and BBC reported he tied the strikes to the Apache incident and to broader frustration with the talks.

nodes.title: Iran says it will 'not hesitate' to defend itself
nodes.what: Iranian officials declared on June 10 that Tehran would 'not hesitate' to defend itself after the latest exchanges with US forces, and accused Washington of a 'calculated war crime' over the strikes. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned the same day of the risk of a new full-scale war across the Gulf.

nodes.title: Gulf states assert right to collective response
nodes.what: Gulf Cooperation Council states issued a joint declaration on June 10 asserting their right to a collective response to Iranian attacks. The statement landed as US-Iran strikes intensified and as Washington signaled, through media briefings, that it hoped the exchanges would not derail a separate deal track.

nodes.title: Israeli strikes kill 16 in south Lebanon; UN to probe
nodes.what: Israeli airstrikes across south Lebanon killed at least 16 people on June 10, including two in a drone strike on a car in Sidon, according to Lebanese sources. The UN announced it would probe alleged international law violations. Lebanon's health ministry put the cumulative death toll from Israeli strikes at 3,696.

nodes.title: Further Israeli strikes on Lebanon as US recovers Apache crew
nodes.what: Israeli airstrikes killed more people in southern Lebanon on June 11 while US forces completed the recovery of the Apache helicopter crew from the Hormuz area. Coverage framed the day as a continuation of intensifying US-Iran exchanges alongside the Lebanon front, with Trump threatening further attacks on Iran as the ceasefire track teetered.

bands.label: Regional war widens
bands.summary: Israel-Hezbollah fighting escalates into open war on the Lebanon front, direct Iran-Israel exchanges break the proxy ceiling and the US is drawn from backstop into active strikes.

nodes.title: Drone strike on Tower 22 kills three US soldiers
nodes.what: A one-way attack drone hit a small US logistics base known as Tower 22 in northeast Jordan, near the Syria-Iraq border, killing three American service members and wounding dozens. US officials attributed the attack to Iran-backed militias operating under the Islamic Resistance in Iraq umbrella. Washington responded days later with strikes on dozens of sites in Iraq and Syria linked to those groups and to Iran's Quds Force.

nodes.title: Iran launches first direct attack on Israel from its territory
nodes.what: Iran fired more than 300 drones, cruise missiles and ballistic missiles at Israel from Iranian soil, framed as retaliation for an April 1 strike on the Iranian consular compound in Damascus that killed senior IRGC officers. Most projectiles were intercepted by Israeli air defenses, US and UK aircraft and regional partners, with limited damage at an airbase in the Negev. Israel struck back on April 19 with a limited hit near Isfahan, signaling capability without a wider exchange.
nodes.disputed: US and Israeli briefings describe the barrage as an unprovoked Iranian escalation requiring a measured response; Iranian and several non-aligned outlets describe it as a calibrated reply to the Damascus consulate strike, which they treat as the initiating act.

nodes.title: Hamas political chief Ismail Haniyeh killed in Tehran
nodes.what: Ismail Haniyeh, the head of Hamas's political bureau and lead Gaza ceasefire negotiator, was killed by an explosion in a guesthouse in Tehran where he was staying after attending the inauguration of Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. Iran and Hamas blamed Israel; Israeli officials did not publicly claim the operation at the time. Tehran vowed retaliation, raising fears of a direct Iran-Israel exchange weeks before Hezbollah commander Fuad Shukr was killed in a separate Israeli strike on Beirut's southern suburbs.

nodes.title: Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah killed in Beirut strike
nodes.what: Israeli aircraft dropped a large number of heavy bombs on a complex in Beirut's southern Dahieh suburb, killing Hezbollah secretary-general Hassan Nasrallah along with other senior commanders. The strike followed days of intensified Israeli air operations across south Lebanon and the Bekaa. Within days Israel announced limited ground operations into south Lebanon, and Iran said it would respond directly.

nodes.title: Iran fires second direct missile barrage at Israel
nodes.what: Iran launched roughly 180 to 200 ballistic missiles at Israel, citing the killings of Nasrallah, Haniyeh and IRGC general Abbas Nilforoushan. Israeli, US and allied air defenses intercepted many missiles, but impacts were reported at air bases and in central Israel, with one Palestinian man killed in the West Bank by falling debris. On October 26 Israel struck military and missile-production sites in Iran in response, while Israeli ground forces pushed into villages in south Lebanon.

nodes.title: Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire takes effect in Lebanon
nodes.what: A US- and France-brokered ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah came into force, calling for a 60-day phased Israeli withdrawal from south Lebanon, the redeployment of the Lebanese army south of the Litani and the dismantling of Hezbollah infrastructure in the border zone. Both sides reported violations within hours, and Israeli strikes on alleged Hezbollah movements continued through 2025 even as the formal truce held. The Gaza war and Houthi strikes on shipping continued, keeping the wider regional confrontation active.

bands.label: Gaza war opens northern front
bands.summary: Hamas's Oct 7 attack triggers the Gaza war and Hezbollah opens a cross-border front in solidarity, pulling Lebanon, Iran-backed groups and US forces in the region into a widening confrontation.

nodes.title: Hamas-led attack on southern Israel
nodes.what: Hamas fighters and allied factions broke through the Gaza perimeter in a coordinated cross-border assault, killing about 1,200 people in Israeli communities and music festival sites and taking some 250 hostages back into Gaza. Israel declared war the same day and began heavy aerial bombardment of the Gaza Strip. The attack reset the regional security map and is the event most Western and Israeli accounts treat as the start of the wider war.

nodes.title: Drone strike on Tower 22 base kills US soldiers in Jordan
nodes.what: A one-way attack drone struck a US logistics outpost known as Tower 22 near the Jordan-Syria border, killing three US Army Reserve soldiers and wounding dozens. US officials attributed the strike to an Iran-backed militia umbrella operating from Iraq and Syria, and the Biden administration ordered retaliatory air strikes on multiple sites days later. The incident marked the first US service-member deaths in the post-Oct 7 escalation.

nodes.title: Strike on Iranian consular annex in Damascus
nodes.what: An air strike destroyed a building beside the Iranian embassy in Damascus, killing senior Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander Mohammad Reza Zahedi and several other officers. Iran blamed Israel and vowed retaliation, while Israel did not formally claim the strike. The attack became the trigger Iran cited for its first openly acknowledged direct strike on Israeli territory.

nodes.title: Iran launches direct drone and missile barrage at Israel
nodes.what: Iran fired more than 300 drones, cruise missiles and ballistic missiles at Israel in its first openly acknowledged direct attack from Iranian soil, citing the Damascus consulate strike as justification. Israel, with US, UK, French and Jordanian assistance, intercepted the bulk of the projectiles, and Israel carried out a limited retaliatory strike near Isfahan days later. The exchange broke a long-standing taboo against direct state-on-state strikes between the two countries.

nodes.title: Pager and walkie-talkie blasts across Lebanon
nodes.what: Thousands of pagers carried by Hezbollah members detonated near-simultaneously across Lebanon and parts of Syria, followed a day later by a wave of exploding walkie-talkies, killing dozens including civilians and wounding thousands. Lebanese authorities and Hezbollah blamed Israel for a supply-chain operation embedding explosives in the devices. The attacks were followed within days by intensified Israeli air strikes on south Lebanon and Beirut's southern suburbs.

nodes.title: Israeli strike kills Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah
nodes.what: Israeli aircraft dropped a heavy bomb load on an underground command complex in Beirut's Dahiyeh suburb, killing Hezbollah secretary-general Hassan Nasrallah and several senior commanders. Hezbollah confirmed his death the next day, and Iran's supreme leader declared a period of mourning. The strike was followed by an Israeli ground incursion into south Lebanon and a sharp escalation that carried the war into 2025.

bands.label: Post-2006 deterrence
bands.summary: After the 2006 Israel-Hezbollah war and Lebanon blockade, an uneasy deterrence holds along the Blue Line while Hezbollah's arsenal grows, Iran's nuclear file hardens and US-Iran sanctions cycles deepen.

nodes.title: 2006 Israel-Hezbollah war begins
nodes.what: After Hezbollah fighters crossed the Blue Line, killed Israeli soldiers and seized two more in a cross-border raid, Israel launched a 34-day air and ground campaign in Lebanon and imposed an air and sea blockade. The war ended with UN Security Council Resolution 1701 and an expanded UNIFIL deployment in the south.

nodes.title: UN Security Council imposes new Iran sanctions
nodes.what: The Security Council adopted Resolution 1929, tightening sanctions on Iran over its nuclear program, expanding asset freezes and adding restrictions on arms transfers and Revolutionary Guard entities. The vote followed years of failed talks over uranium enrichment and IAEA reporting.

nodes.title: Syrian war opens new front for Hezbollah and Iran
nodes.what: Protests in Syria turned into an armed conflict that drew in Hezbollah fighters and Iranian Revolutionary Guard advisers in support of the Assad government, while the United States and Gulf states backed parts of the opposition. The war reshaped Hezbollah's combat experience and arsenal and brought Iranian forces close to the Israeli-held Golan.

nodes.title: United States withdraws from the JCPOA
nodes.what: President Donald Trump announced US withdrawal from the nuclear deal and the reimposition of sanctions on Iran under a maximum pressure policy. European parties said they would try to preserve the agreement; Iran later began rolling back its enrichment limits.

nodes.title: Cross-border fire flares from Lebanon before Oct 7
nodes.what: In April 2023, rocket fire from Lebanon into northern Israel drew Israeli air and artillery strikes, in one of the largest exchanges along the Blue Line since 2006. UNIFIL urged restraint as Hezbollah, Palestinian factions in Lebanon and Israeli forces traded accusations, foreshadowing the wider escalation later that year.

bands.label: Rupture and proxies
bands.summary: The Iranian revolution and embassy crisis rupture US-Iran ties, Israel's 1982 invasion of Lebanon and the rise of Hezbollah set the proxy architecture, and Iraq wars cement US military presence across the Gulf.

nodes.title: Iranian revolution topples the Shah
nodes.what: Mass protests and a general strike forced Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi from power, and Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini returned from exile to lead a new Islamic Republic. The revolution ended decades of close US-Iran alignment and reorganized Iran's security, judicial and clerical institutions under velayat-e faqih.

nodes.title: US embassy in Tehran seized
nodes.what: Iranian students stormed the US embassy in Tehran and held 52 American diplomats and citizens for 444 days. Washington broke diplomatic relations with Tehran in April 1980 and imposed sanctions, beginning a rupture that has never been formally repaired.

nodes.title: Iraq invades Iran, opening eight-year war
nodes.what: Saddam Hussein's forces crossed into Khuzestan, triggering a war that ran until 1988 and killed hundreds of thousands. The United States tilted toward Baghdad over the course of the conflict while also selling arms to Tehran in the Iran-Contra affair, and the Gulf became a theater of tanker attacks and US naval escorts.

nodes.title: Gulf War ends with permanent US presence in the region
nodes.what: A US-led coalition expelled Iraqi forces from Kuwait after Saddam Hussein's August 1990 invasion. The war left American troops, airbases and naval forces stationed across Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar, and the Fifth Fleet headquarters was reactivated in Bahrain in 1995.

nodes.title: Israel withdraws from south Lebanon
nodes.what: Israeli forces pulled out of the security zone they had occupied in south Lebanon since 1985, and the United Nations later certified the line of withdrawal as the Blue Line. Hezbollah claimed the withdrawal as a military victory and consolidated political and armed control across the south.

nodes.title: US-led invasion of Iraq
nodes.what: The United States and United Kingdom launched the invasion of Iraq, toppling Saddam Hussein within weeks and beginning a years-long occupation. The war removed Iran's main regional rival, opened space for Iran-aligned Shia parties and militias in Baghdad, and stationed tens of thousands of US troops on Iran's western border.
